After beating Inter in the derby on Saturday night, AC Milan are hoping that they can ride the wave and get back on track in Europe.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Milan want to rediscover their ‘international DNA’ and put behind them a start to the Europa League campaign that has seen one win and two defeats in the first three games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While it is not yet a do-or-die situation for Ruben Amorim and his squad, failing to secure a win against the Hungarian side – who have a perfect record so far – would make reaching the top 24 significantly more difficult, and a top-eight finish nearly impossible.

Given that the Rossoneri have won seven Champions League titles, no other team in this European competition can boast such a trophy cabinet. Furthermore, the Portuguese manager reached the final with Manchester United two editions ago, ultimately losing to Tottenham.

Consequently, Milan and Amorim must ‘honour’ the Europa League in a manner far removed from their last away outing, which was a heavy defeat against European debutants Bournemouth, with Mike Maignan getting sent off.

This evening over 50,000 fans are expected at San Siro, including a sold-out away sector of 4,200, with over 5,000 Hungarian fans in total throughout the stadium. Milan must secure a victory, channelling the enthusiasm currently felt at Milanello following Saturday’s derby win.

The former United manager tried to brush it aside so his squad could focus solely on the Europa League, but the atmosphere during the final training session was as upbeat as it gets, with lots of ‘slaps’ of congratulations dished out.

Koni De Winter was patted on the back in celebration of his daughter’s birth, Diego Moreira was praised for his goal in the derby, Sankhoun Diawara was acknowledged for his debut(s), and even coach Carlos Fernandes got some love for the corner routine leading to Adrien Rabiot’s goal.

😂 A lot of slaps were given out before training: De Winter for the birth of his daughter, Pulisic for his renewal, Diawara for his debut and Carlos Fernandes for the corner routine leading to Rabiot’s goal ❤️🖤

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 4, 2026

The enthusiasm following the derby must now be channelled into focus and determination ahead of the Europa League return. Milan cannot afford another embarrassing performance in European competition, like those seen against Benfica and Bournemouth.

The club’s storied history forbids it, and Gerry Cardinale certainly wouldn’t welcome a repeat of those displays against the Portuguese or English sides. For this reason, while rotating the squad with an eye on Sunday’s match in Genoa, Amorim will ensure the team retains some key pillars.

De Winter will remain in defence, Yunus Musah and Rabiot in midfield, and Goncalo Ramos in attack. Compared to Saturday’s lineup, there will be seven changes including a forced one in goal, with Lorenzo Torriani replacing the suspended Maignan. Ardon Jashari steps in for Luka Modrić, who will be rested.

With six players sidelined due to injury, the scope for rotation is limited. Yet, even while fielding a side with a significantly lower average age than the one that played in the derby (23.6 years versus 28.1), Amorim has opted not to throw 18-year-olds Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto into the XI.

His goal is to help Gonçalo Ramos – who hasn’t managed a single shot on target in his last two appearances – regain his scoring touch. Consequently, Camarda will have to wait a little longer. As for Comotto, the midfield requires experience, and both Rabiot and Musah are too vital to be left out.

Across the 2024-25 Champions League and the current Europa League campaign, the Rossoneri have won only one of their last six matches, hardly the kind of record expected from a club with such a storied continental past.

According to UEFA, a win in the Europa League is worth €450,000 (with €150,000 for a draw), figures that pale in comparison to the rewards for similar results in the Champions League (€2.1m and €700k, respectively).

The total earnings at the end of each competition are also incomparable: Champions League finalists can rake in between €120m and €125m, whereas the winner of the Europa League can earn, at most, just over €40m.

However, securing the second-tier European trophy guarantees direct qualification for the 2027-28 Champions League, bypassing the need to finish in the top four of Serie A. It also grants a spot in the UEFA Super Cup, which awards €4m to each of the two participating clubs.

Returning to the Champions League – a major objective that was not achieved last season – must be achieved this year, not least for the sake of sponsorships and brand value, two areas of great importance to Cardinale.

Ultimately, the goal is to win a trophy, ideally the Scudetto. However, adding the Europa League title to the trophy cabinet would certainly be a welcome achievement, especially given Milan didn’t win it when it was the UEFA Cup either.

Crystal Palace were unsuccessful in their appeal of the red card Jean-Philippe Mateta received against Tottenham

Mateta was dismissed following a VAR review on his late challenge on Micky van de Ven

When advising on the decision, Gillett said: 'Point of contact is on the achilles, nowhere near the ball. He’s sprinting at speed and with intensity, the studs catch him flush on the achilles. I think it ticks all the boxes for serious foul play.'

Oliver then said over the tannoy: 'After review, Crystal Palace No.14 makes full, forceful contact with the studs on his opponent's achilles. The final decision is red card.’

Sky Sports’ ref watch panel, former referee Dermot Gallagher, Tim Sherwood and Jay Boothroyd, unanimously agreed on Monday that a red card was the correct call.

#1861. Next Crystal Palace manager: Thomas Tuchel’s stance on Anthony Barry is clear amid Pierre Sage uncertainty

By Oliver Thomas | 06 Nov 2026 17:00

England manager Thomas Tuchel has responded to speculation linking his assistant coach Anthony Barry with the Crystal Palace job.

Barry, 40, is reportedly among the frontrunners to succeed current Eagles boss Pierre Sage if the struggling Selhurst Park outfit decide to relieve the Frenchman of his duties.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner in June, but his Crystal Palace side currently sit inside the Premier League relegation zone after losing six of their opening nine games and conceding a division-high 21 goals.

Should the Eagles lose at home to Liverpool on Sunday, the club’s hierarchy may have a big decision to make over whether to stick with under-pressure Sage or bring in a fresh face to turn the club’s fortunes around.

While Tuchel - who announced his latest England squad on Friday - is hopeful that Barry will remain his number two, he is not surprised to see the “highest-level coach” linked with Premier League clubs.

“He’s very important to me,” the German told BBC Radio 5 Live. “I mean, that’s why I did everything I could to convince him to join my staff once we met in Chelsea and join me on my way to Bayern Munich and then in the national team.

“It’s a privilege for me to have him by my side. He’s challenging me, he’s helping me, he makes me better.

“He’s just a fantastic person and the highest-level coach, so I am not surprised that there are rumours around him. I’m not surprised if there were like possibilities for him.”

Barry’s contract with the Football Association runs until the end of the European Championship in 2028 when England will co-host the tournament.

“My understanding, my wish is, of course, that we stay together until minimum until the Euros,” Tuchel added.

“For me, we are by far not finished, and he will always have a place in my in my coaching staff, also after the Euros.

“But, listen, he has to follow also his own path. At the moment, I think that we are an excellent team, and I think that he feels that he’s in a good place where he wants to be.

“As soon as this changes, I think I will be the first to know. At the moment, I don’t know nothing, so I’m pretty confident that he’s in a good place, but I’m not surprised that he has offers.”

Although Barry has never been a senior first-team manager before, he has a wealth of experience as an assistant coach, predominantly working under Tuchel at Chelsea, Bayern Munich and now England.

The Liverpudlian began his coaching career at Accrington Stanley and Wigan Athletic, while he also gained international experience with the Republic of Ireland, Belgium and Portugal, working under Roberto Martinez with the latter two nations.

As well as Barry, Sean Dyche, Thomas Frank, Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards have been linked with the Crystal Palace job amid uncertainty over Sage’s long-term future.

#1858. Why Unai Emery is right to turn down Manchester United and stick with Aston Villa

It’s a great quirk of Premier League scheduling that Manchester United welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford this weekend, after a week in which Jamie Carragher’s suggestion that Villa manager Unai Emery would jump at the chance to move to United prompted a legal threat from the midlands club, an apology from the outspoken pundit and an announcement late on Wednesday that Emery and his bosses had ‘positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club’.

A new contract is reportedly imminent for the Spaniard, and who could possibly blame Emery for sticking around at a club that have repeatedly backed him, given him more control than he’ll have anywhere else and whose fans worship him for delivering their first trophy in 30 years last season.

The alternative? Joining a constant catastrophe that everyone agrees needs far more than just a new manager to put back together.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

While Emery is going nowhere, the whole affair does raise questions about football’s food chain, something which definitely does exist but is clearly going through some changes right now.

Managers will always believe they are the right person to take a once great club and bring back the glory days, and being the one to do so is an intoxicating idea.

But Emery has been here before and was burned by his experience at Arsenal where a collection of expensive failed transfers and unmotivated senior players gave him the worst possible platform to build from. Sound familiar?

All roads still lead to Real Madrid for players but the money involved in Premier League football means simply being a relatively successful English club puts you closer to the top of the chain than ever before, and given United’s penchant for finding new lows every season, a move from Villa north to Manchester is at best a sideways move these days – just ask Youri Tielemans.

Also, given the relative state of flux that many of the ‘big six’ find themselves in these days, there’s an opportunity for Emery and Villa to elbow their way in and become a more established fixture towards the top of the league.

Select your team for football news tailored to you Close

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United are joined by Spurs in their ability to self-implode, Chelsea are chaotic at the best of times, Liverpool are still just about managing the transition to a Jurgen Klopp-less existence and Manchester City are unlikely to be challenging for titles in the near future, depending on impending sanctions.

Only Arsenal are properly set up for consistent success, and Villa clearly believe trusting in Emery is the best way to eventually get themselves into the title conversation.

There are pitfalls to their approach – if Emery does someday get his head turned by a massive paycheck in Saudi Arabia or Real Madrid do come calling, he may still move on and leave the club as a ship without a sail, which is why clubs like Brighton and Brentford treat their managers as cogs in a well-oiled system.

United fans had some temporary relief midweek with their emotional comeback against Roma in the Champions League and may well go into the international break feeling good if they manage to squeeze out a win on Sunday, but regardless of the result, Emery is in the right place.

#1856. Man United injury news: Michael Carrick blow, Liverpool boost as key star set to miss Anfield game after international break

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 17:07

Manchester United's Carlos Baleba will miss his side's clash with fierce rivals Liverpool after the international break, Michael Carrick has confirmed.

The Red Devils are set to face Aston Villa on Sunday in the Premier League, but they know they will be without key players for that clash.

Baleba was forced off in the second half of his side's game against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury.

In a press conference, Carrick confirmed that the midfielder would be out for a considerable period, and that he would be on the treatment table beyond the international break.

That news will come as a significant blow to United, who have to face Liverpool at Anfield on November 22 in the Premier League.

Carrick did not give an exact timeline on Baleba's recovery, but he did reveal that he would miss weeks of action.

United have to face Liverpool after the international break, before taking on Sporting Lisbon three days later in Europe.

Before the start of December, the Red Devils also have to take on Brentford, while the club will also face Newcastle United, Coventry City and RB Leipzig in the first eight days of next month.

Carrick's side end December with fixtures against Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, though perhaps Baleba would be ready to feature in at least some of those games.

United finished in third place last season with 71 points, 11 more than Liverpool managed, and the Merseysiders were arguably fortunate to accumulate as many as they did.

However, a loss against Villa and a defeat at Anfield could leave the Red Devils trailing their rivals by 14 points after just 11 matchweeks.

Baleba is arguably Carrick's only competent midfielder without the ball, and missing him at Anfield makes taking any points from that match much more challenging.

United's inability to make the most of the fact that Liverpool and several other teams like Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea and Manchester City are in transition is concerning.

Losing against Liverpool would compound the failure of the club's hierarchy, and it would arguably be one of the darkest chapters in United's modern history if a loss dropped them into the relegation zone.

#1855. Arsenal urged to avoid £64m transfer mistake after Micah Richards claim

Arsenal should be wary of selling Viktor Gyokeres in the January transfer window, according to former Gunners striker Jeremie Aliadiere.

Gyokeres produced his best performance of the season in midweek with a goal and an assist to help the Gunners beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the Champions League.

But it has otherwise proved to be a frustrating few months for the Swede, who has started just one Premier League match for Mikel Arteta’s side so far this season.

Gyokeres amassed a respectable 21 goals in all competitions in his maiden season after arriving from Sporting CP for £64million, but now faces an uncertain future at the Emirates having fallen beneath Kai Havertz in the pecking order.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

With speculation likely to mount ahead of the January window, some pundits, including Micah Richards, have suggested that the Gunners should look to move Gyokeres on.

But former Arsenal striker Aliadiere believes that might be a mistake and ultimately leave Arteta short of options at the top of the pitch.

‘I think it’s all depending on the finances how much they can get for him and who to replace him with,’ Aliadiere told Metro.

‘Because I think as much as obviously he’s not in the top 11 now because Havertz is preferred number one, you don’t want to sell him, get a good price and not be able to replace him.

‘If Havertz gets injured, which obviously we’ve seen in the past – he’s had a few injuries and he can pick up injuries – you just end up with no striker at all.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So I think it’s a very difficult January transfer window. Do you try to buy someone before you sell? I think when you look over the summer, selling Trossard and Martinelli before buying somebody.

‘Obviously, they go to Tzolis, but I’m not sure Tzolis was bought to be the first choice and when he is injured, you end up doing Eze on the left-hand side, and that’s not really his best position in my opinion.

‘So I don’t want it to happen with Gyokeres, thinking let’s try to sell him and recuperate a good transfer fee for him and then not replacing him.’

But even if Gyokeres remains at the club, Aliadiere can’t envisage the 28-year-old becoming the long-term solution to Arsenal’s search for a clinical striker.

‘I just feel the way Arsenal plays does not quite suit Gyokeres’ style of play,’ Aliadiere, speaking via football betting, added.

‘I’ve always been very quite patient and looking at the good stuff that he does, and I still feel that he does some amazing work. But I just do feel that the players don’t really give him the ball quick enough, which is what he needs.

‘He needs to be on 1v1. He needs to run the channel, get fed the ball quite quickly. And I feel we’re not really playing that way. We like to control the ball.

‘We like to control the tempo and just slow down the game. And I just feel Gyokeres is more of a counter-attacking player where he sees the space, he wants it quickly and then he’s on 1v1 and then he can then dominate physically.

‘But he’s rarely getting in that position, so I just find it difficult to kind of see him turning things around in a way of probably just being a rotation player.’

#1854. Inside Mason Greenwood's new life in Turkey ahead of Liverpool clash: How former Man United star has stayed under the radar, why Fenerbahce fans have welcomed him - and his new luxurious gated community

Published: 05:18 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 06:46 EDT, 4 November 2026

If you're choosing a club to keep a low profile – the claustrophobic fervour of Fenerbahce seems a strange option.

But Mason Greenwood – since being mobbed by fans at Istanbul Airport with his partner Harriet Robson and two young daughters in the summer – has tried to fly under the radar.

From Man United prodigy to club-hopping pariah on a European exile, the 25-year-old hasn't found a comfortable home in three years since leaving his homeland.

A reminder of the why... Early in 2022, Greenwood was arrested and later charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm.

Those charges were subsequently dropped but after a six-month internal Man United investigation into his conduct, the club agreed he could not continue to ply his trade at Old Trafford.

Greenwood's attempt at career resurrection took him on loan to Getafe and later a turbulent two years in Marseille before Fenerbahce broke their transfer record to snap him up for £33million.

Former Man United star Mason Greenwood joined Fenerbahce from Marseille in the summer

Greenwood has largely tried to fly under the radar alongside his partner and two daughters

Greenwood has found a home in Istanbul's luxury gated district of Sariyer (pictured above with the all-female team of estate agents who helped him with the purchase)

While there was noisy resistance to Greenwood joining Marseille, he found no such opposition in Turkey, where one prominent journalist claimed 95 per cent of the population would not know or care about his past.

He didn't face any questions about the dropped charges or his public image in his first press conference and outside of brief post-match comments, has not conducted any interviews of note.

Greenwood has been hiding from the limelight a record signing would usually bask in, especially in the football-crazed city of Istanbul.

He found a home in a district called Sarıyer, a favourite among footballers, who largely live in gated communities.

Sarıyer is located on the eastern side of the city towards luxurious Black Sea beaches and quieter historic towns.

Greenwood is said to count team-mates N'Golo Kante and Marco Asensio as neighbours and was seen in a rare online post after securing his new home, posing with the all-female team of estate agents who helped him with the purchase.

Since the big-money move, Greenwood has only posted four times on his Instagram profile, all of which were generic action shots after matches.

In his latest offering, accompanied by snaps from his different clubs, he wrote: 'From my first professional goal to number 100. Different clubs, different countries, so many memories along the way. A special milestone for me.'

His partner, Harriet, is also selective with how much she shares from their new life.

She only has four posts in total, with around 20 photos in each 'round-up', offering a glimpse into the high-life, though Greenwood himself only appears twice.

One of the images is of him looking exhausted in hospital at the birth of their second daughter in 2023 and another shows him holding hands with their eldest, Summer, who is three.

Sariyer is located on the eastern side of Istanbul towards the Black Sea beaches and quieter historic towns - and away from the mayhem of the city's centre

Greenwood and his partner Harriet are cautious in what they share but one image (pictured above) shows him looking exhausted in hospital at the birth of their second daughter in 2023

The forward will be hoping to make an impact when Fenerbahce take on Liverpool this evening

Greenwood's engagement through new media and traditional remains deliberately cautious.

He's slipped into a quiet life in the suburbs, punctuated by the intense matchday experience at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

So far, Greenwood has made 11 goal contributions in 18 matches for his new side, an impressive return, particularly with the club enduring a turbulent start to the season.

He missed Fenerbahce's defeat at the weekend after suffering with a virus but ex-Liverpool cult hero Dirk Kuyt – who is interim manager – is expecting him to be available for the most high-profile match of the season so far.

Turkey has provided an unchallenging and comfortable new home for Greenwood. For many watching him on Wednesday night, the overriding feeling may still be one of unease.

#1851. MN: 11 defeats in 20 for Allegri – why the Cagliari loss may have been a blessing for Milan

A report this morning has put forward the notion that it may be a blessing in disguise that AC Milan missed out on the Champions League.

MilanNews write that the club ‘have Cagliari to thank for that May day at San Siro’. It’s paradoxical, following an initial instinctive reaction: how can Milan hosting Ferencvaros be better than facing PSG, Barcelona ​​or Manchester City on a magical Champions League night?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Well, considering how Massimiliano Allegri is doing with Napoli, there is a compelling case that it was necessary pain. The report explained the thesis.

Allegri’s decline began on 15 March 2026, the day of the 1-0 defeat away against Lazio after he won the derby thanks to Pervis Estupinan’s goal. It takes us to 4 November 2026, the date of Porto 4-1 Napoli, that latest terrible result from the coach.

It seems that bad results constant tension in the dressing room have followed Max in the past few months. In this block of 20 matches between Milan and Napoli, Allegri’s difficulty is evident, with a decidedly negative record of 11 defeats against only six wins and three draws.

Furthermore, 31 goals conceded in 20 matches is enormous for teams historically led by a pragmatic and defensive manager like the Livorno-born manager. Essentially, since that derby won with that surreal goal from Estupinan, ‘Allegrismo’ has only meant disasters.

The feeling is that if Milan had celebrated their return to the Champions League they would have kept Allegri, but in the long run they would have wasted another year chasing a style of football and a way of managing the club that no longer seems viable.

Less than 24 hours after the Cagliari game, there was a clear-out of the management as Gerry Cardinale saw fit to launch yet another revolution. It takes time and patience, but perhaps it’s better this way, to feel like something is genuinely being built towards.

Without Giorgio Furlani as CEO, the club will be entrusted to a competent and experienced Head of Football (likely to be Markus Krösche, a director with obvious pedigree). With Ruben Amorim at the helm, we can expect to see a more modern and entertaining style.

There are of course inconsistencies to iron out, and the squad must be improved, but we must question what would have been lost had Cagliari not made history that night at San Siro.

#1847. Aston Villa news: Unai Emery reveals latest on contract talks ahead of Man United showdown

By Darren Plant | 06 Nov 2026 17:37

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has admitted that discussions over a new contract have been "very positive".

Emery and his squad are currently preparing to face Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday.

There had been the potential for a huge sub-plot, with the Red Devils' hierarchy known to be admirers of the Spaniard.

However, Emery will take his place in the Villa dugout at the Theatre of Dreams having made it clear that he has no interest in replacing Michael Carrick.

Meanwhile, Villa revealed earlier this week that they have held extensive talks with the 54-year-old over plans for the long-term future.

Speaking at a press conference, Emery hinted that it may only be a matter of time before he extends his contract past 2029.

He told reporters: "I had a good meeting with [chairman] Nassef Sawiris, very positive, so let's talk next week, trying to get everything we spoke about together in a deal.

"My vision is to keep our consistency and how we are improving, how we are building a lot of things positively; being strong, keeping it consistent in our process. It's a huge challenge, but the club is involved in it.

"After speaking with us last year, they decided to build a new stand, adding more supporters in Villa Park. It's one clear step forward to getting better.

"We are increasing our budget each year, increasing our revenue through our performance, playing in Europe, improving players, selling players, then buying young, talented players.

"This is the process of the vision we should keep in our future."

For all of the recent positivity at Villa Park, Emery's side have gone three matches without a win in all competitions.

With Villa already four points adrift of fourth place in the Premier League table, they can ill-afford more dropped points against Man United.

Carrick's side, who are deemed to be in disarray, can move to within two points of Villa with a second high-profile triumph this week, after they beat Roma on Tuesday.

#1846. New pope, rise of Luke Littler and what that has happened since Spurs last won four games in a row

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

It has been 1,108 days since Tottenham last won four Premier League games in a row - a run they could end this weekend when they face Leeds at Elland Road.

Not since the opening months of Ange Postecoglou’s reign have Spurs won more than three times in succession - a feat they quickly achieved twice either side of a north London derby draw under the Australian between August and October 2023 - and a lot has happened in the intervening three years.

That season, fast-starting Tottenham won eight of their first 10 fixtures and went five points clear at the summit despite the high-profile summer loss of Harry Kane to Bayern Munich, eventually finishing in fifth place.

Here, Standard Sport looks at some of the biggest stories to have happened since Spurs last won four on the bounce.

Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost was elected as the 267th Pope of the Catholic Church in May 2025, taking the name Pope Leo XIV.

While Pope Leo is said to be a Real Madrid fan, he was gifted a Sunderland shirt with the name "Pope Leo, 14" emblazoned on the back ahead of the club’s Europa League campaign.

Pope Leo was gifted the shirt after Sunderland’s chaplain, Father Marc Lyden-Smith, gave one to Pope Francis ahead of the Black Cats’ victory over Newcastle in 2013.

Donald Trump was re-elected as President of the United States in November 2024, defeating Democratic candidate and former vice-president Kamala Harris.

It came four years after Mr Trump had lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden, ending his initial spell in the White House after victory over Hillary Clinton in 2016.

The Labour Party came back into power after 14 years as Sir Keir Starmer was elected as UK Prime Minister in July 2024.

Despite a landslide victory, Starmer resigned in July 2026 and was replaced by Andy Burnham.

The UK has now had five Prime Ministers in the last five years.

Daniel Levy stepped down as executive chairman of Tottenham in September 2025, bringing to an end his 25-year reign at the club.

Following Levy’s departure, non-executive chairman Peter Charrington declared “a new era of leadership for the club” before Spurs went on to endure their worst season in Premier League history as they only narrowly avoided relegation to the Championship on the final day.

Tottenham would have been relegated had they not mustered up a nervy 1-0 win at home to Everton on the final day of last season.

Man City XI vs Nottm Forest: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

Tottenham XI vs Leeds: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

Where to watch Leeds vs Tottenham: TV channel and live stream

12 months after lifting the Europa League, their first major trophy for 17 years, Spurs would remarkably become mired in a relegation battle with rivals West Ham, staying up by the skin of their teeth thanks to a goal from loanee Joao Palhinha.

Spurs’ decision to get rid of Postecoglou just 16 days after he guided them to Europa League success over Manchester United in Bilbao was always going to prove controversial.

No one, though, could have foreseen the disaster that would unfurl over the next season as Tottenham went through three managerial changes in 10 months.

Thomas Frank was brought in as Postecoglou’s successor, but was eventually sacked in February 2026 with the club hovering over the relegation zone.

His replacement, Igor Tudor, lasted just 44 days before the club hit the panic button again to bring in Roberto De Zerbi to steer them to safety.

In the space of three years, West Ham went from Conference League winners to being relegated to the Championship.

A series of poor recruitment decisions, managerial changes and ownership uncertainty ensured the Hammers failed to build on their first piece of major silverware in 43 years before eventually dropping back to the second tier after 14 seasons.

Darts sensation Luke Littler announced himself on the biggest stage at just 16 years old as he made a historic run to the World Championship final on his debut at Alexandra Palace in January 2024.

Since then, Littler has become a back-to-back world champion and underlined his place as the best player on the planet while still a teenager.

Another sporting prodigy, Kimi Antonelli has risen from obscurity to the top of his sport in the last three years.

At just 20 years and 68 days old, Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula One world champion in history on Sunday after clinching the 2026 title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

A record-breaking campaign has also seen Antonelli become the youngest winner of the Monaco Grand Prix, the youngest driver to achieve a Grand Slam, and the first Italian in more than 60 years to be crowned world champion.

Sir Andy Murray and Rafael Nadal retired within a few months of each other to leave Novak Djokovic as the last man standing from the ‘Big Four’ era of 21st century tennis.

Two-time Wimbledon winner Murray retired in August 2024 and was swiftly followed by 22-time Grand Slam champion Nadal in October. It followed Roger Federer’s retirement in September 2022.

Boxing fans have long since grown weary of Tyson Fury’s retirement U-turns, so his fourth announcement last year that he was hanging up his gloves convinced few. Just a handful of months later, he made the decision to step back into the ring for a fifth, and surely, final time in April 2026.

The former world heavyweight champion beat Russian Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous decision in his first fight back and is now gearing up for a hotly-anticipated bout with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff in December, having also defeated Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

Manchester United Carlos Baleba is not expected to return until December at the earliest after suffering a hamstring injury.

The summer signing was forced off early in the second-half of Tuesday’s Champions League game against Roma.

The former Brighton star made a bursting run into the box but pulled up just as he was about to pull the trigger on goal.

Baleba appeared to be in tears as he limped off the Old Trafford pitch. Having already missed the opening five games of the campaign as a result of an ankle injury he suffered during pre-season with Brighton, he now faces another spell on the sidelines.

#1844. Fans fume at referee Andy Madley caught laughing and joking with Arsenal stars at half-time of win at Liverpool

Published: 06:03 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 07:58 EDT, 4 November 2026

Liverpool fans are fuming after referee Andy Madley laughed and joked with Arsenal's stars at half-time of their clash on Sunday – having denied them a penalty.

The Gunners claimed their first victory at Anfield since September 2012 thanks to Kai Havertz's goal, with the win sending Mikel Arteta's side three points clear of Manchester City.

But Reds supporters came away fuming after being denied a seeming stonewall penalty in the first half when Jurrien Timber tugged back Alexander Isak.

Isak had a golden chance to equalise when he rose to meet Bradley Barcola's cross, only to miss the ball after having his shirt pulled by Timber.

The Arsenal defender avoided punishment from Madley and VAR decided against intervening despite the vehement protests of Andoni Iraola and his players.

It was therefore extra galling for Liverpool fans to see the referee appearing to tell a joke to Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, and Declan Rice at half-time – though of course the encounter could have been entirely innocent.

Liverpool fans are fuming after referee Andy Madley was caught laughing and joking with Arsenal's players - having denied the Reds a penalty

Liverpool were denied a penalty after Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt

Fans claim Madley shouldn't have been cracking jokes with the Premier League champions

Part of refereeing, after all, is maintaining a relationship with players.

But for Liverpool it is another twist of the knife after a painful defeat which saw them fail to score from 18 shots and left them fifth in the Premier League.

'This referee clearly had a favourite. Liverpool got robbed in broad daylight,' one fan said on X.

'At any level of the game from Sunday pub league to Premier League, referees shouldn't be laughing and joking and high-fiving players on any side. They should turn up, ref neutrally, go home,' another said.

'He should not ref any more Arsenal games,' one added.

There is no evidence that Madley is biased towards the Premier League champions.

Sky Sports pundits Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright unanimously agreed Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty at half-time and suggested that Isak was denied the spot-kick because he failed to make more of the incident.

Iraola thinks the game could have gone differently had Madley not missed Timber's shirt pull.

The Liverpool boss said after the match: ‘There are two situations and they are a little bit related. The Isak one is a clear penalty.

‘He's gonna head the ball in front of the goal, and they grab him where everyone sees the shirt. You don't need a lot, just to avoid Alex, because the ball just goes in front of him, and I don't see the reason why, probably because he doesn't dive or he doesn't go to the floor. It shouldn't be a reason not to concede a penalty.'

Liverpool were irate as they lost to Arsenal at home for the first time since September 2012

Iraola also pointed to a similar situation where Cody Gakpo was tugged back, but the officials said the Dutchman would not get to the ball.

‘They say the ball was too long and Cody wouldn't have arrived to the ball, but then you're basically accepting that the first one is, is a pen, no?’ added Iraola. ‘So you cannot use the argument in both ways differently. So I think it's a, yes, it's a pen, the Alex one is.’

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, the manager said: 'It's a problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor. The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

'It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it.'

Asked if he will tell Isak to do that in future, the Spaniard replied: 'Yes, definitely.'

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk took aim at VAR too after the match, expressing his disappointment at the defeat.

'I think it was a clear penalty. I've seen it back and I've seen it being given. Today it wasn't meant to be,' he said.

Asked if Isak should have reacted more, the Dutchman added: 'We have 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras?

'Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal.'

Former Liverpool defender Carragher was furious that VAR had not intervened as he analysed the incident at half-time.

'One of the best goal-scorers in the league is pulled back seven yards from goal, and the pull back stops him heading the ball. Why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job,' he said bluntly.

Arsenal moved to the top of the table on 24 points with victory at Anfield, while Liverpool remained fifth after Brighton and Chelsea, who are third and fourth respectively, both won on Saturday.

Mikel Arteta hailed his side’s resilience to win at Anfield.

Asked if it feels better to do so as a player or manager, he said: ‘Now it feels better as a manager, it has been such a long time without this feeling. We are extremely proud, especially the conditions we arrived in after the defeat against Fleetwood looked like the end of the world.

‘But then you have to pick yourself up. Four days later you have to come to Anfield against this manager and this team.’

#1842. Manchester United have a new wildcard manager target with Michael Carrick sack decision imminent

Manchester United are considering several candidates as they assess their options for the managerial position, but there are reservations about a number of the names linked with the job.

Eddie Howe has for some time been considered the frontrunner for the role, should Michael Carrick get sacked, but The Independent report that the former Newcastle manager is less highly regarded by Man Utd than other reports have suggested.

Julian Nagelsmann is the other highly prominent name, though his reputation has suffered following his time at Bayern Munich and with the Germany national team. Man Utd’s interest is said to be driven by the club’s recruitment chief, Christoph Vivell, but others are less convinced amid concerns over Nagelsmann's relationship with players during his time with the national team.

The same concerns court Antonio Conte, who would bring considerable experience, having won league titles with four different clubs, but have seen many of his previous jobs end in acrimony. The Independent adds that there are doubts that Man Utd’s squad is strong enough to meet the Italian’s demands.

A move for Didier Deschamps reportedly failed earlier in the week, with the former France head coach reluctant to return to club management.

A new wildcard name in the frame is Stuttgart manager Sebastian Hoeness, who his appointment would be considered another big gamble after the likes of Ruben Amorim failed spectacularly. The Independent also mention Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler, but it is feared he could find it difficult to replicate his success on the south coast should he move to Old Trafford.

Como manager Cesc Fabregas is considered highly unlikely, with Arsenal reportedly viewing him as a potential long-term successor to Mikel Arteta.

Carrick staying has also not been ruled out. The same report notes that Man Utd’s decision-making has partly been influenced by performance data, which points to narrow margins and missed chances having contributed to Man Utd languishing around the relegation zone.

Up next is an Aston Villa who are firing on all cylinders under Unai Emery, but have won just once at Old Trafford in 15 years. The win over Roma in midweek has offered somewhat of a reprieve, but another damaging result on Sunday could still spell the end of Carrick.

A decision on Carrick’s future is expected to come during the international break.

#1839. Chelsea news: Xabi Alonso reacts to Cole Palmer's England squad omission, Thomas Tuchel comments

By Darren Plant | 06 Nov 2026 17:37

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has suggested that he has little interest in Cole Palmer's ongoing situation with England.

With five goals and three assists from 11 appearances in 2026-27, the 24-year-old can be relatively pleased with his start to the season.

However, after withdrawing from England's squad for their September and October fixtures due to either a minor injury or to manage his workload, the playmaker is in the bad books of Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel.

After leaving Palmer out of his latest squad on Friday, the German reiterated that the player is paying the price for 'missed opportunities' to impress.

Despite the perceived disappointment of one of his key players, Alonso hinted at a press conference on Friday that he does not get himself involved with national team matters.

He told reporters: "No. We have not spoken about that. We have been talking about our game on Sunday."

"We are focussed on our things, on Chelsea things and how to do better and how to help him and how he can become more and more influential on the game. Those are our topics to talk."

Having continued to be pressed on the subject, Alonso reiterated: "We speak about Chelsea. We have enough on our plate. My impact area is my control area and what we talk about."

The assumption is that Palmer will feel disappointed having missed out on another opportunity to represent England.

Despite the mixed reports that came out about the reasoning being his withdrawal last time, Tuchel has clearly been left unimpressed.

JJ Gabriel has revealed the key motivation behind his impending move to Real Madrid after turning his back on Manchester United.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, but has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

And in a brief interview with the Spanish outlet Marca, Gabriel revealed he has one particular goal in mind for his time at Real.

Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he moves closer to joining Real Madrid.

The teenager has already spent time training in Barcelona before moving to the Spanish capital, where his representative Ali Barat is handling negotiations and helping arrange accommodation for Gabriel and his family.

His Irish passport is expected to make a move to Spain possible under FIFA regulations allowing certain players aged 16 to 18 to transfer within the European Union. However, Gabriel remains registered with United, meaning he cannot yet represent another club.

United are disappointed to lose one of their highly-rated academy prospects and had attempted to persuade him to stay by offering a new contract and a pathway towards senior football.

The club could receive training compensation if the transfer is completed, with reports suggesting the figure could be around £350,000.

Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut and was named Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season last term.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It wasn’t a very well-kept secret that the Portuguese was under pressure, and it didn’t take long until Sergio Conceicao replaced him in what seemed to be a manoeuvre orchestrated mainly by agent Jorge Mendes.

“I think there was a phone call. It happened around the time the rumours started circulating that Rui had refused to speak to me.

#1831. New footage shows how goalkeeper in Spanish footballer's killer collision was fired-up in moments before 'reckless' tackle - as police probe medical team after opening homicide investigation

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and NATALIA PENZA

Published: 05:13 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:28 EDT, 4 November 2026

New footage has revealed the tense moments before goalkeeper Jesus Owono launched a 'reckless' tackle that led to the death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker De Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

A homicide squad has launched an investigation as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation, with police now also probing the medical response to the incident.

Now, new footage taken from the stands has revealed how a fired-up Owono behaved in the moments leading up to the devastating collision.

The video shows how Owono had made his way to the other end of the pitch to get involved in a confrontation following a red card for opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, before appearing to motion for him to make his way off the field of play.

Footage has revealed the heated build-up to the tackle that led to the death of Jesus de Miguel, which showed goalkeeper Jesus Owono arguing with his rival goalkeeper. (Source: X/Eldense_)

Fans have commented in Owono's involvement in an argument with opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, who was sent off in the closing stages of the match (Source: X/Eldense_)

Martin and Owono appeared to continue their argument as they exchanged gestures as the Tenerife shot-stopper departed the scene.

The footage then captured Owono's wild celebrations - in which he leapt into the air and punched his fist - as Andorra FC scored an 88th minute equaliser.

'Here you have the images prior to the action by goalkeeper Owono, in the parts where he's not in focus — in one of them, he's confronting and saying things to the rival goalkeeper, and in the other, celebrating the goal right in the face of the Tenerife stands,' one fan wrote.

'He's a repeat offender when it comes to this kind of behavior.'

Another said: 'There isn't anyone from those of us who were in the stadium who didn't agree with the opinion that the entry was reckless. That it was an assault. It's clear that he didn't want the final outcome, but it's also clear that it wasn't an isolated incident.'

'I'm right behind that goal! Owono was completely unhinged! He came all the way to the rival goal to confront Dani, the Tenerife goalkeeper, over Lautaro's red card, and started gesticulating wildly at Dani to get him off the field after being sent off! This guy was totally out of his mind,' a third posted.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

De Miguel died on Tuesday morning following a horrifying clash with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

Andorra FC defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected’ by the tragedy.

‘There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,’ Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

‘What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

‘First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch,' he said.

‘I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

‘In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether Jesus de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died yesterday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his second-division club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

Police investigating the death of CD Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel are probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono

Well-placed sources told local press overnight there were 'certain discrepancies within the reports, or potential inaccuracies when compared to other evidence in the case' such as video footage recorded and posted on social media.

Respected island newspaper El Dia said: 'Among the issues currently under investigation, which according to sources remained unresolved as of yesterday, is whether the medical team who rushed from the sidelines to the centre of the pitch carrying a stretcher, a spinal board, and an Automated External Defibrillator to attend to the player, acted with due diligence during the more than six minutes they spent on the pitch before placing him on the spinal board for transport to an ambulance, which was stationed at one of the stadium access gates on La Mutine Street.'

It added: 'Investigators are also looking into an even more striking question.

'After a Guedel airway, a curved, semi-rigid oropharyngeal tube, was inserted into the player's mouth following his loss of consciousness, to prevent his tongue from obstructing his airway, was he also provided with oxygen during the resuscitation efforts on the pitch, as is required by protocol?

'According to sources, efforts are still underway to gather all available evidence to determine whether De Miguel was administered oxygen, either via a bag-valve mask (Ambu bag) or a face mask connected to one of the oxygen cylinders kept pitchside at the stadium.

'Sources indicate that this remains unresolved, at least regarding the medical care provided on the field of play.

'Furthermore, footage of the player being transported on a spinal board suggests that oxygen was not being administered during that process.

'Additionally, during the evacuation from the centre of the pitch to the ambulance, the player was carried on a spinal board by individuals who were moving at a jog.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel outside the entrance to Tenerife's stadium

'The manner in which the patient was transported, which should never have been carried out in such a way, was highly dangerous to their physical well-being.'

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who has lived in Spain since he was eight, was red-carded for kneeing Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel in the chest near the halfway line late into stoppage time. The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

Tragic Jesus, whose partner Maria and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time yesterday morning he had died at a hospital in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz about 8am, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats'.

It said in a statement, after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened: 'Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats, and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, which occurred this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8am.

'There are no words of comfort, there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow.

'We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire 'tinerfeñismo' community, who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Owono is reportedly intending to apologise directly to de Miguel's family for his challenge and has made his social media private following abusive chants and messages he received (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Owono is reportedly seeking to apologise to Jesus de Miguel's family before making any kind of public statement.

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said yesterday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

Later today Jesus de Miguel's body is expected to be flown to the Spanish mainland so his funeral can take place in the town where his parents hail from.

The 30-year-old footballer's mum and dad travelled to Tenerife after being told about the severity of his injuries before confirmation this morning he had died in an island hospital.

They will now make the reverse trip to Madrid before travelling to Navahermosa in the province of Toledo 80 miles south-west of the Spanish capital which they have chosen as the place for the player's funeral.

Jesus's club revealed the location yesterday afternoon but said it was unable to say at this stage when exactly it would be.

Town hall officials in Navahermosa, which has a population of just over 3,500 inhabitants, said immediately after learning of the footballer's death: 'Since yesterday, we had held onto the hope that Jesus might overcome the toughest match of his life. However, we woke up today to the worst possible news.

'On behalf of the town hall, we wish to express our deepest sorrow at this tragic outcome. We want to extend all our love, support, and affection to his family, friends, and everyone who is feeling this loss today.

'There are no words that can ease such profound pain, but please know that we are by your side and that we share in your sadness.

'Jesus, you have always been, and will always remain, a source of pride for us.

'Today, with broken hearts, we must say goodbye, but we will hold onto your memory. Rest in peace.'

Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of Spain's Castilla-La Mancha region which includes Navahermosa and the province of Toledo where a train crash last Wednesday claimed the lives of 69 people, added in his own statement: 'I am at a loss for words; the passing of footballer Jesus de Miguel, while doing what he loved most and what he had fought so hard for, playing football, is heartbreaking news.

'My thoughts are with his family, who hail from the municipality of Navahermosa in the province of Toledo. My deepest condolences.'

The entire CD Tenerife squad will travel to Navahermosa to pay their last respects to their teammate.

Flags outside the town hall flew at half mast today.

The National Police in the island capital Santa Cruz has yet to release an official statement about its ongoing probe.

A minute's silence was held before Champions League matches in memory of De Miguel on Tuesday

But a force spokesman said yesterday evening: 'An investigation is underway into the circumstances surrounding the incident which led to Jesus de Miguel's death which is being conducted by the homicide unit.

'It has been opened because the death was not the result of natural causes and it will seek to determine whether in terms of the law, an involuntary manslaughter could have been committed.'

The report police draft as a result of their probe will be submitted to a local judge whose job it will be to decide whether to take the matter further.

A Canary Islands court source described the collision between the two footballers as 'an accidental collision on the playing field.'

But he added: 'Any death not resulting from natural causes, referred to as a 'forensic death,' whether due to an accident or other factors, automatically triggers a judicial investigation, which is the case here.'

Court officials said this morning they weren't able to comment on when they expected to receive the police report into the drama.

One said: 'At the moment the investigation is still in the hands of police who will submit their report to a court in Santa Cruz once officers have completed their work.'

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham will be sweating over the fitness of Mathys Tel during the international break after the forward was forced off against Leeds on Saturday.

In a potentially significant injury blow, the French forward was substituted before half-time after a heavy challenge from Jayden Bogle, who landed his studs on the the Spurs man’s left Achilles.

Tel initially tried to continue before signalling to the Spurs bench that he could not play on, and he was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute.

Bogle was not booked by the referee, John Brooks, and while VAR reviewed the challenge, they did not deem it to meet the threshold for serious foul play.

In a feisty opening 45, Bogle escaped a booking, much to the frustration of Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, who remonstrated with fourth official Josh Smith on the touchline.

#1817. Celtic legend Frank McAvennie forced to apologise after labelling star's decision to miss games following his father's death as 'woke nonsense'

Published: 07:06 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:29 EDT, 4 November 2026

Former Scotland forward Frank McAvennie has apologised after describing Auston Trusty’s extended absence following his father's death as 'woke nonsense'.

Trusty announced the death of his father Walt last month, with the United States' international sharing a touching tribute on Instagram.

The 28-year-old has since sat out matches against Celta Vigo, Hibernian, Dundee United and Falkirk.

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill, speaking prior to the match against Falkirk on Sunday, confirmed Trusty was still yet to return as he was 'celebrating the life of his dad'.

Celtic subsequently fell to a shock 2-0 defeat to Falkirk, with O'Neill's side having won just one of their four matches in Trusty's absence.

McAvennie, who scored 37 goals in 85 games across two spells with Celtic, questioned the length of Trusty's absence following the bereavement.

Auston Trusty announced the death of his father Walt in an emotional Instagram post last month. (Source: Instagram/austontrusty3)

Ex-Celtic forward Frank McAvennie has apologised after labelling Trusty's absence as 'woke' on his podcast as he claimed the defender had to 'get on with it'. (Source: Let Me Be Frank podcast)

Trusty thanked his father for his 'guidance and unwavering dedication to our family' on social media and stated he would 'spend my life trying to make you proud'. (Source: Instagram/austontrusty3)

'I've got every respect for that, but how long do you want off?' McAvennie said on his Let Me Be Frank Podcast.

'Martin says he's away to celebrate the life of his dad. Celebrate the life? You've got football. You're getting paid and we're in trouble. How long is it going to be?

'It’s the woke brigade now, isn’t it? It’s nonsense. My dad was the best man, the only man I looked up to when he died, but you’ve got to get on with it.'

McAvennie has since apologised after a backlash to his remarks, with the 66-year-old admitting 'I should have chosen my words more carefully.'

'I've seen some of the reaction to comments I made on the podcast about Auston's absence from football following the death of his father,' McAvennie said.

'I can understand why people feel my comments were insensitive, and looking back, I should have chosen my words more carefully.

'Everyone deals with grief differently, and I certainly meant no disrespect to Auston or his family.

'Celtic need the big man back, and that's what I was clumsily trying to say. I wish him and his family all the very best.'

Trusty has missed Celtic's last four matches following the death of his father last month

McAvennie was part of the Celtic side that won the Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup in the 1987-88 season. He scored both of Celtic's goals in a 2-1 victory over Dundee United in the cup final.

The forward also helped West Ham secure promotion in 1991 during the second of his two spells with the Hammers.

McAvennie sold medals he won to Celtic-supporting businessman Lord Willie Haughey in 2000, after facing financial difficulties having appeared in court in a drugs trial that year.

He was ultimately cleared in court of conspiring to deal £110,000 worth of amphetamines and ecstasy. McAvennie had pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine, his second such offence.

McAvennie avoided jail but he was given a two-year conditional discharge and ordered to pay costs.

A separate incident saw McAvennie receive a four-month suspended jail sentence in 2009 after he admitted to headbutting a 23-year-old man outside a bar on the Isle of Man following an altercation.

The former forward, who had admitted to making mistakes during his career and expressed regret over his use of cocaine during his career, had his medals returned to him by Haughey in 2017.

Despite their recent run of form, Celtic are currently four points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, although nearest rivals Rangers have a game in hand.

O'Neill's side are next in action in the Europa League on Thursday when they face Turkish side Besiktas.

Celtic have lost all three of the league phase matches in the competition so far this season.

#1816. Barcelona's 'new De Bruyne' impresses alongside Lamine Yamal

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 17:39

Barcelona have found an unexpected solution to their defensive injury crisis in a young midfielder once compared to Kevin De Bruyne, whose remarkable relationship with Lamine Yamal is now proving valuable to Hansi Flick.

Brian Fariñas, 20, has impressed in his first two senior appearances for the Catalan giants, operating at right-back despite spending most of his development at La Masia in midfield.

The academy graduate made his competitive debut in Barcelona's 6-1 victory over Alaves on October 31 before retaining his place for Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League success against Aston Villa.

His performances have already earned praise from Flick, but a new account from his former youth coach has revealed an intriguing story behind his development.

Fariñas was once nicknamed 'Fabruyne' because of his technical qualities, while his close friendship with Yamal stretches back to their earliest years together in Barcelona's academy.

Fariñas joined Barcelona's youth system in 2018, arriving as a relatively shy youngster before gradually establishing himself as one of La Masia's most promising midfielders.

His development took an important turn when he began playing alongside Yamal in the club's youth teams.

Iván Carrasco, the coach who first brought the pair together, has revealed that the two became virtually inseparable.

"They were like two peas in a pod. They used to get up to all sorts of mischief at La Masia," Carrasco told Mundo Deportivo.

"They went everywhere together. They were always playing jokes in the dressing room. They developed a really good connection and have got on brilliantly ever since."

Their friendship continued even as their careers progressed at different speeds.

Yamal made his first-team breakthrough at 15 and quickly established himself among Barcelona's most important players, while Fariñas continued developing in the academy.

The latter regularly attended matches at Camp Nou in the seats reserved for players' relatives and friends, and even travelled to Germany to watch Yamal help Spain win Euro 2024.

Carrasco also revealed that Fariñas possessed attacking qualities that earned him an unusual nickname during his youth career.

"I used to call him 'Fabruyne'," the former Barcelona coach explained, referring to Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne.

The comparison came from Fariñas's ability to use both feet, move inside from wide areas and strike powerfully from distance.

"He can use both feet, which is very interesting when you're playing on your natural side. He can cut inside and shoot with his left," Carrasco added.

"He has a stepover that you'll see plenty of. It's like the one De Bruyne used to do."

The former coach believes Barcelona supporters have yet to see the full range of Fariñas's attacking abilities, particularly his shooting from outside the penalty area.

Originally developed as an attacking midfielder, the youngster also featured on the wing before gradually moving into deeper midfield positions.

He was an important member of Barcelona's Under-19 side that completed a domestic and European treble in 2024-25, before establishing himself with Barça Atlètic under Juliano Belletti.

Last season, he contributed five goals and six assists in 35 appearances for the reserve team.

Those performances helped convince Flick that Fariñas deserved a place in his senior plans, with the German reportedly intervening during the summer to prevent a proposed move to Girona.

Fariñas's route into Barcelona's starting lineup has been particularly surprising because the opportunity arrived in a position he had rarely occupied.

Injuries to Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart left Flick with limited defensive options ahead of the Alaves match.

Rather than selecting a more experienced player out of position, the Barcelona manager handed Fariñas his senior debut at right-back.

Fariñas completed 100 of his 103 passes against Alaves, recorded 114 touches and demonstrated impressive composure despite facing unfamiliar defensive responsibilities.

His ability to move forward and combine with Yamal also caught Flick's attention.

"He connects very well with Lamine. That's very important," the German explained after the victory.

"He helped us a lot in that position. He deserved these minutes because he's very professional and always focused in training."

Fariñas himself acknowledged the significance of the support he received from his teammates, particularly Yamal.

"They gave me confidence," he said after his debut, referring to the assistance provided by the players around him.

Four days later, Flick retained the youngster against Aston Villa, giving him a first Champions League appearance against Premier League opposition.

Fariñas again looked comfortable in possession, completing 11 passes in the attacking third, a figure matching Pedri's contribution in that area.

His understanding with Yamal helped Barcelona maintain attacking combinations down the right without sacrificing the defensive discipline required of a full-back.

The partnership represents an unusual reunion for two players who once operated together much further forward in La Masia.

While Yamal has become one of the world's most exciting wingers, his childhood friend is now providing support from behind him.

With Kounde still recovering from an ankle problem, Fariñas could receive another opportunity when Barcelona visit Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

Flick has not suggested that the youngster will permanently replace the French international, but his emergence gives the German another option in a defence repeatedly disrupted by injuries.

For a player once known for his resemblance to De Bruyne, the chance to establish himself at the highest level may have arrived in a position few expected.

#1814. Roberto De Zerbi knows Tottenham's biggest issue and has the blueprint to fix it

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham’s winning run was always likely to be tested at an amped up Elland Road, but they head into the international break with plenty to consider after a tepid attacking display was punished late on by Leeds substitute Noah Okafor.

Spurs player ratings vs Leeds: Flop defender lucky not to be sent off

Tottenham hit with huge injury blow as Leeds 'escape red card'

Tottenham XI vs Leeds: Starting lineup and confirmed team news

Choose the right education path for your child

Despite failing to hold on for a third successive clean sheet, Spurs’ defence can come away with their heads held high, having handled Leeds’ intensity well for large periods.

It is Spurs’ attack that Roberto De Zerbi will be most disappointed with, as his side failed to create any real chances of note, bar Jan Paul van Hecke’s late header, allowing Leeds to push on and take control of the game.

Spurs were always going to have to suffer here, but the fact they did not have an out-ball meant Leeds felt comfortable keeping the pressure on and committing more bodies forward in search of the opening goal.

It was the hosts who asked all the questions, and eventually their dominance told as Okafor collected the ball inside the area and fired past Antonin Kinsky with a little over 10 minutes to play.

Spurs lack a focal point in attack, with the lively Mathys Tel forced off through injury early on and both Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke struggling to assert themselves. The latter pair managed a combined four touches in the opposition box.

Compare that with the battling performance of Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who beat Van Hecke in the air to set in motion Leeds’ opener, and you begin to see where the issue lies.

Spurs spent heavily over the summer, but it is clear they still need to invest in a centre-forward. Solanke has struggled for form and fitness over the last 12 months, while Marmoush is an awkward profile and certainly not cut out to lead the line as the lone striker in De Zerbi’s system.

Spurs returned from the last international break revitalised, and De Zerbi will be glad to have more time on the training ground to iron out his side’s attacking deficiencies.

There was no lack of resilience or application from Spurs today, but they were ultimately let down by the fact that they could not make the ball stick in the final third.

With Spurs frequently turning over possession, Leeds were able to keep hammering away at the visitors’ resolve, and it was inevitable they would capitalise sooner rather than later.

This result is a blip rather than a call for crisis. Spurs have been much improved over the last few weeks, and on another day they would have kept Leeds at bay and celebrated a well-deserved clean sheet.

What their performance highlighted, though, is just how much they miss James Maddison and still long for a striker in the image of Harry Kane.

Yusuf spoke at a press conference on the eve of the match against Milan alongside head coach Borbely Balazs. The forward echoes the words if his manager, speaking of the great opportunity a night like this presents.

You have made many sacrifices to get to San Siro…

“When I think back to where I started, it’s truly extraordinary that I can play against one of the best clubs in the world this Thursday. It’s the result of a huge amount of effort, and I’m quite proud of what I’ve achieved. I hope this journey continues for a long time to come.”

Amorim picked you out specifically as a threat to Milan. How does this make you feel? And what is your preferred role?

“Compliments are nice. It means I’m probably doing things the right way. For me, it makes no difference whether I play as a winger or a striker. In both positions, I always try to give my all and have fun on the pitch. It’s certainly significant that a coach of his calibre has mentioned me.”

Did you analyse Milan’s derby win over Inter?

“They played an intense match against Inter, and we analysed the match in detail. However, we can’t draw conclusions based on how the derby unfolded. I’m curious to see how these ninety minutes unfold.”
